mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals robust labor market conditions that historically correlate with rising corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months with PAYEMS growth exceeding 100k, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 0.5% for two consecutive months, it signals the onset of monetary tightening, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as equity valuations face pressure from higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signal a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as corporate revenue expectations are revised downward.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months with both HOUST and RSAFS declining, or the Rank IC for the interaction term falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, as defined by three consecutive months of rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS), S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days are typically negative due to reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs suppressing corporate investment.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months during tightening cycles, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing and industrial activity, which historically correlates with rising corporate profits and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months with INDPRO growth exceeding 0.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.5%, it signals a tight labor market that typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as strong employment supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months with UNRATE below 3.5%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeds 2.0% and monthly CPI (CPIAUCSL) remains below 3.0%, it signals strong economic expansion without excessive inflation, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings growth is sustained without monetary policy tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of months with GDPC1 > 2.0% and CPIAUCSL < 3.0%, or the Rank IC for the interaction term falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, as defined by housing starts (HOUST) above 1700 thousand units, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days are typically negative due to the risk of overbuilding and subsequent correction in the housing sector.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of months with HOUST above 1700 during late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.
